column2: On the authority of Abū Dharr Jundub ibn Junādah and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Muʿādh ibn Jabal (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both), from the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace), who said:

“Fear Allah wherever you are; follow a bad deed with a good deed and it will wipe it out; and treat people with good character.” Reported by al-Tirmidhī, who said: A ḥasan hadith; in some copies: ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
Ittaqi Allāh (“fear Allah”): by carrying out His command, avoiding what He has forbidden and stopping at His limits.
Ḥaythumā kunta (“wherever you are”): in whatever place you are, where people see you and where they do not, for He is watching you.
Wa-atbiʿ (“follow”): with hamzah, sukūn on the double-dotted tāʾ and kasrah on the single-dotted bāʾ; [it means] attach.
Al-sayyiʾah (“a bad deed”): leaving some obligation or committing something prohibited.
Al-ḥasanah (“a good deed”): repentance from it,
Tamḥuhā (“it will wipe it out”): wipe out its punishment from the records of the angels and its bad effect on the heart.
Wa-khāliqi al-nās (“and treat people”): deal with them
bi-khuluqin ḥasan (“with good character”): that is, do for them what you would like them to do for you; by this hearts are united, people agree and affairs are set in order.
The command to fear Allah, which is Allah's counsel to all His creation and the Messenger's ﷺ counsel to his nation.
Doing a good deed after a bad deed wipes out the bad deed.

This is part of Allah the Exalted's favour to His servant, for there will inevitably be shortcomings in his taqwā at times, either by leaving some of what is commanded or committing some of what is prohibited; so Allah commanded him to do what wipes out that shortcoming, namely to follow it with a good deed.

Encouragement to good character, which is one of the qualities of taqwā without which taqwā is not complete. It is mentioned separately only because of the need to make it clear, for many people think that taqwā is merely fulfilling the rights of Allah without the rights of His servants;
but that is not so. Rather, combining the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants is what the Sharīʿah requires, and it is rare: only those who have attained perfection are equal to it.
